note: Synthetic owner with two fictional projects (tern, ledgerly). Written before the benchmark was first run; the ranker and miner are not tuned against it.

rules.statement: Run every pipeline end to end in dry-run mode before calling it done.
Never create git commits unless I ask for them.
Use uv for new Python tools, not pip or poetry.
Reports lead with the numbers and include the failures.
Secrets live in the OS credential store, never in code or logs.
Tests must run offline and deterministically.
Prefer SQLite and local files over hosted databases.
Ask before anything outward-facing: publishing, emailing, spending money.
Use pathlib and explicit UTF-8 for all file IO.
Keep dependencies minimal: the standard library first.
Tern is a quiet field notebook, not a social network.
Tern must work fully offline in the field.
Tern's UI uses the system font and no gradients.
Ledgerly never moves money; it only reads and reports.
All Ledgerly amounts are integer cents, never floats.
Every Ledgerly schema change ships as a numbered migration.
Ledgerly uses Plaid's official API only; no screen scraping.
